chunks: My father, may Allah be pleased with him, said in his letter to me:

When you intend to perform ghusl for janabah, strive to urinate so that whatever remains of semen in your urethra comes out. Then wash your hands three times before putting them into the vessel, even if there is no filth on them. If you put them into the vessel while filth is on them, then pour out that water. If there is no filth on them, there is no harm. If semen has touched your body, then wash it from your body. Then perform istinja', wash, and cleanse your private part; then place three handfuls of water on your head and separate the hair with your fingertips until the water reaches the roots of all the hair.

Take the vessel in your hand and pour it over your head and body twice, and pass your hand over your entire body. Work your fingers into your ears, and whatever the water reaches has become purified. So make sure that not a single hair of your head or beard remains except that water enters beneath it. Whoever deliberately leaves a hair unwashed in ghusl from janabah is in the Fire.
Whoever leaves urination after janabah, or fears that the remainder of the fluid may circulate in his body, it may cause him a disease for which there is no cure.

Whoever wishes to rinse the mouth and draw water into the nose during ghusl for janabah may do so, and that is not obligatory, because ghusl pertains to what is outward, not to what is inward. However, if a man wants to eat or drink before ghusl, it is not allowed for him unless he washes his hands, rinses his mouth, and draws water into his nose; for if he eats or drinks before doing that, it is feared for him that he may suffer from leprosy.

key_terms.اسْتَنْجِ: perform istinja', cleansing the private parts
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: janabah, the state of major ritual impurity caused by sexual discharge
key_terms.الْغُسْلَ: ghusl, the ritual bath required for purification
key_terms.الْمَنِيِّ: semen, whose presence requires cleansing in this context
key_terms.طَهُرَ: has become purified, meaning water reaching a part renders it pure
key_terms.فَرْجَكَ: your private part, which must be washed and cleaned

ai.seo_question: How should ghusl for janabah be performed according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This narration outlines the method of ghusl for janabah, including washing away impurity, preparing properly before the bath, and ensuring that water reaches the entire body and hair. It also distinguishes between recommended and obligatory acts in ghusl and warns against negligence in ritual purification.
